records.literal_gloss: And said Yahweh to me, take for yourself a tablet large and write on it with [the] stylus of a man, for Maher-shalal-hash-baz.

en.B: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} said to me, "Get yourself a large tablet and write on it in ordinary letters, 'Belonging to Maher-shalal-hash-baz.'
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} said to me, "Get a large tablet. On it, write in plain letters that anyone can read: 'For Maher-shalal-hash-baz.'

es.B: {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} me dijo: «Consíguete una tablilla grande y escribe en ella con letras comunes: ‘Perteneciente a Maher-salal-has-baz’.
es.R: {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} me dijo: «Consigue una tablilla grande. Escribe en ella con letras sencillas que cualquiera pueda leer: ‘Para Maher-salal-has-baz’.

decisions.choice: tablet: a flat surface for public writing
decisions.reason: The word is rare; in 3:23 a related form seems to mean a mirror or a thin sheet. Here it is something large enough to be set up and read in public, a tablet or a sheet.

decisions.choice: a man's stylus: ordinary writing that anyone can read
decisions.reason: "The stylus of a man" most likely means common, everyday script, not the special writing of scribes, so that every passer-by could read the inscription.

decisions.choice: Maher-shalal-hash-baz: "Spoil hurries, plunder hastens"
decisions.reason: The name is made of four words: two verbs of haste and two words for loot. It announces that the enemies of Judah, Damascus and Samaria, will soon be plundered (verse 4). The small word before it marks the tablet as belonging to, or being about, the name.

decisions.choice: in ordinary letters (Balanced); in plain letters that anyone can read (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the sense of the idiom; Literal keeps "a man's stylus".

decisions.choice: Maher-salal-has-baz
decisions.reason: The name is written in the Spanish form the terms note sets, with the Hebrew sh written as s, as in Sear-jasub (7:3).

decisions.choice: "Maher-shalal-hash-bazi"
decisions.reason: The name is kept, in the form set by the terms note; its meaning, "spoil hurries, plunder hastens" (m3), is given in the English notes.

source.text: וְאָעִ֣ידָה לִּ֔י עֵדִ֖ים נֶאֱמָנִ֑ים אֵ֚ת אוּרִיָּ֣ה הַכֹּהֵ֔ן וְאֶת־זְכַרְיָ֖הוּ בֶּ֥ן יְבֶרֶכְיָֽהוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And I will call as witness for myself witnesses reliable, Uriah the priest and Zechariah son of Jeberekiah.

en.L: And I will call reliable witnesses to witness for me, Uriah the priest and Zechariah son of Jeberekiah."
en.B: I will have trustworthy witnesses confirm it for me, Uriah the priest and Zechariah son of Jeberekiah."
en.R: I will have two men you can trust be witnesses for me: Uriah the priest and Zechariah son of Jeberekiah."

es.L: Y tomaré para mí testigos fieles que lo atestigüen: al sacerdote Urías y a Zacarías hijo de Jeberequías».
es.B: Haré que testigos dignos de confianza lo confirmen: el sacerdote Urías y Zacarías hijo de Jeberequías».
es.R: Haré que dos hombres de confianza sean mis testigos: el sacerdote Urías y Zacarías hijo de Jeberequías».

sw.B: Nitawaweka mashahidi wa kuaminika wanithibitishie, Uria kuhani na Zekaria mwana wa Yeberekia."
sw.R: Nitawaweka watu wawili wanaoaminika wawe mashahidi wangu: Uria kuhani na Zekaria mwana wa Yeberekia."

decisions.choice: I will call witnesses: the LORD still speaking, giving the purpose of the writing
alternatives: and I took reliable witnesses (the prophet speaking)
decisions.reason: The verb form follows the commands of verse 1 and can express their purpose: write it, so that I may have it witnessed. Read this way, the LORD is still the speaker. The same form could also be the prophet's own words, "so I called reliable witnesses". The Septuagint has a command, "and make witnesses for me".

decisions.choice: Uriah the priest and Zechariah: known men whose word would be trusted
decisions.reason: Witnesses would later confirm that the name was written before the child was born and before the events it foretold. A priest Uriah served under Ahaz in Jerusalem (2 Kings 16:10-16).

decisions.choice: two men
decisions.reason: Readable names the number of witnesses, which the list makes plain.

records.literal_gloss: And I drew near to the prophetess, and she conceived and she bore a son. And said Yahweh to me, call his name Maher-shalal-hash-baz,

en.L: And I drew near to the prophetess, and she conceived and bore a son. And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to me, "Call his name Maher-shalal-hash-baz.
en.B: I went in to the prophetess, and she became pregnant and bore a son. Then {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to me, "Give him the name Maher-shalal-hash-baz.
en.R: Then I slept with my wife, the prophetess. She became pregnant and had a son. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} told me, "Call him Maher-shalal-hash-baz.

es.L: Y me acerqué a la profetisa, y ella concibió y dio a luz un hijo. Y {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} me dijo: «Ponle por nombre Maher-salal-has-baz.
es.B: Me uní a la profetisa, y ella quedó embarazada y dio a luz un hijo. Entonces {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} me dijo: «Ponle el nombre de Maher-salal-has-baz.
es.R: Luego tuve relaciones con mi esposa, la profetisa. Ella quedó embarazada y tuvo un hijo. {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} me dijo: «Llámalo Maher-salal-has-baz.

sw.L: Nami nikamkaribia nabii mke, naye akapata mimba akazaa mwana. Naye {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akaniambia, "Mwite jina lake Maher-shalal-hash-bazi.
sw.B: Nilimwendea nabii mke, naye akapata mimba akazaa mtoto wa kiume. Ndipo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akaniambia, "Mpe jina Maher-shalal-hash-bazi.
sw.R: Kisha nilikutana kimwili na mke wangu, aliyekuwa nabii. Akapata mimba akazaa mtoto wa kiume. {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akaniambia, "Mwite Maher-shalal-hash-bazi.

decisions.choice: I drew near to: I had marital relations with
decisions.reason: To "draw near" or "go in" to a woman is a polite way to speak of sexual union (Genesis 20:4; Leviticus 18:14).

decisions.choice: the prophetess: Isaiah's wife
alternatives: a woman prophet other than Isaiah's wife
decisions.reason: The woman is not named. She is most likely Isaiah's wife, called "the prophetess" either because she herself prophesied, like Huldah (2 Kings 22:14), or because she was the prophet's wife. She is the mother of this child, who with Shear-jashub (7:3) is one of the signs of verse 18.

decisions.choice: call his name Maher-shalal-hash-baz: the name written on the tablet now given to a child
decisions.reason: The name written before witnesses (verses 1-2) is given to the newborn, so the boy himself becomes a living sign of the message (verse 18), as Immanuel was to be in 7:14.

decisions.choice: my wife
decisions.reason: Readable says who the prophetess is, as the context implies; see the meaning decision on "the prophetess".

source.text: כִּ֗י בְּטֶ֨רֶם֙ יֵדַ֣ע הַנַּ֔עַר קְרֹ֖א אָבִ֣י וְאִמִּ֑י יִשָּׂ֣א׀אֶת־חֵ֣יל דַּמֶּ֗שֶׂק וְאֵת֙ שְׁלַ֣ל שֹׁמְר֔וֹן לִפְנֵ֖י מֶ֥לֶךְ אַשּֽׁוּר׃ס

records.literal_gloss: For before knows the boy to call, my father, and, my mother, will carry off [someone] the wealth of Damascus and the plunder of Samaria before the king of Assyria.

en.L: For before the boy knows [how] to call out 'My father' and 'My mother,' the wealth of Damascus and the plunder of Samaria will be carried off before the king of Assyria."
en.B: For before the child can say 'Father' or 'Mother,' the riches of Damascus and the spoil of Samaria will be hauled away before the king of Assyria."
en.R: Before the boy is old enough to say 'Father' or 'Mother,' the wealth of Damascus and the loot of Samaria will be taken away and brought to the king of Assyria."

es.L: Porque antes de que el niño sepa decir ‘Padre mío’ y ‘Madre mía’, la riqueza de Damasco y el botín de Samaria serán llevados delante del rey de Asiria».
es.B: Porque antes de que el niño sepa decir ‘Papá’ o ‘Mamá’, las riquezas de Damasco y el botín de Samaria serán llevados ante el rey de Asiria».
es.R: Antes de que el niño tenga edad para decir ‘Papá’ o ‘Mamá’, la riqueza de Damasco y el botín de Samaria serán llevados al rey de Asiria».

sw.L: Kwa maana kabla mvulana hajajua kuita 'Baba yangu' na 'Mama yangu,' utajiri wa Dameski na nyara za Samaria zitachukuliwa mbele ya mfalme wa Ashuru."
sw.B: Kwa maana kabla mtoto hajaweza kusema 'Baba' au 'Mama,' utajiri wa Dameski na nyara za Samaria zitachukuliwa na kupelekwa mbele ya mfalme wa Ashuru."
sw.R: Kabla mvulana huyo hajakua kiasi cha kusema 'Baba' au 'Mama,' mali ya Dameski na nyara za Samaria zitachukuliwa na kupelekwa kwa mfalme wa Ashuru."

decisions.choice: before the boy knows: a short span of time, as in 7:15-16
decisions.reason: A child learns to say "father" and "mother" within his first year or two. The sign repeats the time limit given with Immanuel (7:16): before a child is grown, the two kings who threaten Judah will be gone.

decisions.choice: Damascus and Samaria plundered by the king of Assyria
decisions.reason: Damascus was the capital of Aram under Rezin, and Samaria the capital of Israel under Pekah son of Remaliah (7:1). Tiglath-pileser III of Assyria took Damascus in 732 BC and stripped Israel of much of its land (2 Kings 15:29; 16:9); Samaria itself fell in 722 BC.

decisions.choice: someone will carry off: an impersonal verb, best read as passive
decisions.reason: The verb has no named subject ("one will carry off"); the sense is that the wealth will be carried away, brought before the Assyrian king as plunder.

decisions.choice: 'Father' or 'Mother'
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the child's first words without "my"; Literal keeps "My father" and "My mother".

sw.R: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alisema nami tena. Alisema,

decisions.choice: spoke again: a new word from the LORD
decisions.reason: The words "again" and "yet" mark a fresh message, which runs through verse 8.

source.text: יַ֗עַן כִּ֤י מָאַס֙ הָעָ֣ם הַזֶּ֔ה אֵ֚ת מֵ֣י הַשִּׁלֹ֔חַ הַהֹלְכִ֖ים לְאַ֑ט וּמְשׂ֥וֹשׂ אֶת־רְצִ֖ין וּבֶן־רְמַלְיָֽהוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: Because has rejected the people the this the waters of the Shiloah which go gently, and rejoicing with Rezin and the son of Remaliah,

en.L: "Because this people has rejected the waters of Shiloah that flow gently, \q and [there is] rejoicing over Rezin and the son of Remaliah,
en.B: "This people has turned away from the gently flowing waters of Shiloah \q and takes delight in Rezin and the son of Remaliah.
en.R: "These people have rejected the waters of Shiloah, which flow quietly and calmly. \q They are glad about Rezin and the son of Remaliah.

es.L: «Por cuanto este pueblo ha desechado las aguas de Siloé que corren mansamente, \q y [hay] regocijo por Rezín y el hijo de Remalías,
es.B: «Este pueblo ha despreciado las aguas de Siloé, que corren mansamente, \q y se complace en Rezín y en el hijo de Remalías.
es.R: «Esta gente ha rechazado las aguas de Siloé, que corren tranquilas y en calma. \q Se alegran por Rezín y por el hijo de Remalías.

sw.L: "Kwa sababu watu hawa wameyakataa maji ya Shiloa yaendayo polepole, \q na [kuna] kufurahia Resini na mwana wa Remalia,
sw.B: "Watu hawa wameyaacha maji ya Shiloa yatiririkayo taratibu \q na kufurahia Resini na mwana wa Remalia.
sw.R: "Watu hawa wameyakataa maji ya Shiloa, ambayo hutiririka kwa utulivu na amani. \q Wanafurahia Resini na mwana wa Remalia.

decisions.choice: the waters of Shiloah: Jerusalem's quiet water supply, a picture of the LORD's care
decisions.reason: Shiloah was a channel carrying water from the Gihon spring along the side of the city (compare the pool of Siloam, John 9:7). Its slow, quiet stream stands for the LORD's protection of Zion, which Ahaz refused to trust (7:4, 9). It is set against the flood of the great River in verse 7.

decisions.choice: rejoicing with Rezin and the son of Remaliah: delight in the two kings, or joy over them
alternatives: melting in fear before Rezin and the son of Remaliah
decisions.reason: The phrase is hard. It may describe people who welcome the alliance of Rezin and Pekah, or who rejoice at the thought of being rid of them by Assyria's help. Either way they look to human powers instead of the LORD. "This people" may mean Judah, or Israel in the north, which had joined Rezin.

decisions.choice: This people has turned away ... (no "because")
decisions.reason: The "because" clause runs into "therefore" in verse 7. Balanced and Readable state the cause as its own sentence and keep "therefore" in verse 7.

decisions.choice: Siloé
decisions.reason: The Spanish uses the familiar form of the name of Jerusalem's water channel, the same name as the pool of Siloé in John 9:7.

source.text: וְלָכֵ֡ן הִנֵּ֣ה אֲדֹנָי֩ מַעֲלֶ֨ה עֲלֵיהֶ֜ם אֶת־מֵ֣י הַנָּהָ֗ר הָעֲצוּמִים֙ וְהָ֣רַבִּ֔ים אֶת־מֶ֥לֶךְ אַשּׁ֖וּר וְאֶת־כָּל־כְּבוֹד֑וֹ וְעָלָה֙ עַל־כָּל־אֲפִיקָ֔יו וְהָלַ֖ךְ עַל־כָּל־גְּדוֹתָֽיו׃

records.literal_gloss: And therefore, look, [the] Lord [is] about to bring up on them the waters of the River, the mighty and the many, the king of Assyria and all his glory. And it will rise over all its channels and it will go over all its banks.

en.L: therefore, look, the Lord is bringing up upon them the waters of the River, mighty and many, \q the king of Assyria and all his glory. \q And it will rise over all its channels and go over all its banks.
en.B: So now the Lord is about to bring against them the waters of the River, strong and plentiful: \q the king of Assyria and all his glory. \q It will rise over all its channels and spill over all its banks.
en.R: So the Lord will bring a great flood against them, like the waters of the Euphrates River. \q That flood is the king of Assyria, with all his glory and power. \q It will rise and fill every stream and overflow every bank.

es.L: por tanto, he aquí, el Señor hace subir sobre ellos las aguas del Río, impetuosas y abundantes, \q al rey de Asiria con toda su gloria. \q Y subirá sobre todos sus cauces y pasará sobre todas sus riberas.
es.B: Por eso ahora el Señor está a punto de traer contra ellos las aguas del Río, poderosas y abundantes: \q el rey de Asiria con toda su gloria. \q Crecerá por encima de todos sus cauces y se desbordará por todas sus riberas.
es.R: Por eso el Señor traerá contra ellos una gran inundación, como las aguas del río Éufrates. \q Esa inundación es el rey de Asiria, con toda su gloria y su poder. \q Crecerá y llenará cada arroyo y se desbordará por todas las orillas.

sw.L: kwa hiyo, tazama, Bwana analeta juu yao maji ya Mto, yenye nguvu na mengi, \q mfalme wa Ashuru na utukufu wake wote. \q Nayo yatapanda juu ya mifereji yake yote na kupita juu ya kingo zake zote.
sw.B: Kwa hiyo sasa Bwana yu karibu kuleta juu yao maji ya mto Frati, yenye nguvu na mengi: \q mfalme wa Ashuru na utukufu wake wote. \q Yatapanda juu ya mifereji yake yote na kufurika juu ya kingo zake zote.
sw.R: Kwa hiyo Bwana ataleta gharika kubwa juu yao, kama maji ya mto Frati. \q Gharika hiyo ni mfalme wa Ashuru, pamoja na utukufu wake wote na nguvu zake. \q Itapanda na kujaza kila kijito na kufurika juu ya kila ukingo.

decisions.choice: the River: the Euphrates
decisions.reason: "The River" without a name is the Euphrates (Genesis 31:21; 1 Kings 4:21), the great river of Mesopotamia, home of Assyria. Its flood is set against the gentle waters of Shiloah (verse 6).

decisions.choice: the king of Assyria and all his glory: the flood explained
decisions.reason: The prophet names what the picture means: the Assyrian king and the splendor of his army. The power Ahaz hired against Aram and Israel (2 Kings 16:7-9) will overflow onto Judah too.

decisions.choice: the Lord: the title "Lord" (master), not the divine name
decisions.reason: Here the title Adonai, "Lord", stands alone, not the name Yahweh.

decisions.choice: a great flood ... like the waters of the Euphrates River
decisions.reason: Readable names the River and makes the comparison plain. "And power" is added to explain "glory" here, the splendor of an army.

decisions.choice: el Río (L, B); el río Éufrates (R)
decisions.reason: The English B says "the River" here and R names the Euphrates; the Spanish follows each level, with "Río" capitalized at L and B as the name of the great river.

source.text: וְחָלַ֤ף בִּֽיהוּדָה֙ שָׁטַ֣ף וְעָבַ֔ר עַד־צַוָּ֖אר יַגִּ֑יעַ וְהָיָה֙ מֻטּ֣וֹת כְּנָפָ֔יו מְלֹ֥א רֹֽחַב־אַרְצְךָ֖ עִמָּ֥נוּ אֵֽל׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And it will pass on into Judah; it will overflow and pass over; to [the] neck it will reach. And will be the spreadings of its wings [the] fullness of [the] breadth of your land, O Immanuel.

en.L: And it will sweep on into Judah; it will overflow and pass over; \q it will reach up to [the] neck. \q And the spreading of its wings will be the fullness of the breadth of your land, O Immanuel."
en.B: It will surge on into Judah, flooding and passing through until it reaches the neck. \q Its outspread wings will cover the whole width of your land, O Immanuel."
en.R: It will rush on into Judah and flood it until the water is up to the people's necks. \q Like a huge bird with its wings spread out, it will cover your whole land, Immanuel."

es.L: Y pasará hasta Judá; inundará y pasará adelante; \q hasta el cuello llegará. \q Y el despliegue de sus alas llenará la anchura de tu tierra, oh Emanuel».
es.B: Avanzará hacia Judá, inundándola y pasando por ella hasta llegar al cuello. \q Sus alas extendidas cubrirán todo lo ancho de tu tierra, oh Emanuel».
es.R: Se precipitará sobre Judá y la inundará hasta que el agua le llegue a la gente al cuello. \q Como un ave enorme con las alas extendidas, cubrirá toda tu tierra, Emanuel».

sw.L: Nayo yatapita kuingia Yuda; yatafurika na kupita juu; \q yatafika hata [shingoni]. \q Na kunyooshwa kwa mabawa yake kutajaza upana wa nchi yako, Ee Imanueli."
sw.B: Yatafagia kuingia Yuda, yakifurika na kupita hadi yafike shingoni. \q Mabawa yake yaliyokunjuliwa yatafunika upana wote wa nchi yako, Ee Imanueli."
sw.R: Yatakimbilia ndani ya Yuda na kuifurikisha mpaka maji yafike shingoni mwa watu. \q Kama ndege mkubwa aliyekunjua mabawa yake, yataifunika nchi yako yote, Imanueli."

decisions.choice: up to the neck: almost, but not quite, drowning
decisions.reason: A flood up to the neck is deadly danger, yet the head stays above water. Judah will be nearly overwhelmed by Assyria; Jerusalem itself survived in 701 BC (chapters 36-37).

decisions.choice: the spreading of its wings: the flood pictured as a bird with outstretched wings
decisions.reason: The picture shifts from a flood to a bird whose wings stretch over the whole land. The wings may mean the flood's spreading arms, or the army as a bird of prey. Some hear in "wings" a hint of protection (Psalm 91:4), but here the wings cover the land as the invader does.

decisions.choice: your land, O Immanuel: the land belongs to the child of 7:14
decisions.reason: Immanuel means "God is with us" (7:14). The land the Assyrian floods is Immanuel's land; the cry is both a lament and a reminder that God has a claim on it. Verse 10 repeats the words of the name as a confession: "God is with us". Matthew 1:23 applies the name to Jesus.

decisions.choice: the people's necks; Like a huge bird
decisions.reason: Readable says whose neck is meant and makes the picture of the wings a comparison.

source.text: רֹ֤עוּ עַמִּים֙ וָחֹ֔תּוּ וְהַֽאֲזִ֔ינוּ כֹּ֖ל מֶרְחַקֵּי־אָ֑רֶץ הִתְאַזְּר֣וּ וָחֹ֔תּוּ הִֽתְאַזְּר֖וּ וָחֹֽתּוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: Be evil, O peoples, and be shattered, and give ear, all distant places of earth. Gird yourselves, and be shattered; gird yourselves, and be shattered.

en.L: Be evil, peoples, and be shattered! \q And give ear, all distant places of [the] earth! \q Gird yourselves, and be shattered; \q gird yourselves, and be shattered!
en.B: Do your worst, you peoples, and be shattered! \q Listen, all you distant lands! \q Arm for war, and be shattered; \q arm for war, and be shattered!
en.R: You nations, go ahead and do your worst, but you will be crushed! \q Listen, all you lands far away! \q Get ready for battle, but you will be crushed. \q Yes, get ready for battle, and you will still be crushed!

es.L: ¡{{plural_you:Hagan|Haced}} el mal, pueblos, y {{plural_you:sean quebrantados|sed quebrantados}}! \q ¡Y {{plural_you:presten|prestad}} oído, todos los lugares lejanos de la tierra! \q {{plural_you:Cíñanse|Ceñíos}}, y {{plural_you:sean quebrantados|sed quebrantados}}; \q {{plural_you:cíñanse|ceñíos}}, y {{plural_you:sean quebrantados|sed quebrantados}}.
es.B: ¡{{plural_you:Hagan|Haced}} lo peor que puedan, pueblos, y {{plural_you:serán destrozados|seréis destrozados}}! \q ¡{{plural_you:Escuchen|Escuchad}}, todas las tierras lejanas! \q {{plural_you:Ármense|Armaos}} para la guerra, y {{plural_you:serán destrozados|seréis destrozados}}; \q {{plural_you:ármense|armaos}} para la guerra, y {{plural_you:serán destrozados|seréis destrozados}}.
es.R: ¡Naciones, {{plural_you:hagan|haced}} lo peor que puedan, pero {{plural_you:serán aplastadas|seréis aplastadas}}! \q ¡{{plural_you:Escuchen|Escuchad}}, todas las tierras lejanas! \q {{plural_you:Prepárense|Preparaos}} para la batalla, pero {{plural_you:serán aplastadas|seréis aplastadas}}. \q Sí, {{plural_you:prepárense|preparaos}} para la batalla, y aun así {{plural_you:serán aplastadas|seréis aplastadas}}.

sw.B: Fanyeni mabaya yote mnayoweza, enyi mataifa, nanyi mvunjwe! \q Sikilizeni, enyi nchi zote za mbali! \q Jiandaeni kwa vita, nanyi mvunjwe; \q jiandaeni kwa vita, nanyi mvunjwe!
sw.R: Enyi mataifa, endeleeni kufanya mabaya yote mnayoweza, lakini mtapondwa! \q Sikilizeni, enyi nchi zote za mbali! \q Jiandaeni kwa vita, lakini mtapondwa. \q Naam, jiandaeni kwa vita, nanyi bado mtapondwa!

decisions.choice: be evil: do harm, rage (spoken in scorn to the nations)
decisions.reason: The verb may come from a root "be evil" or from one meaning "break"; some read it as "raise the war cry". The Septuagint has "know", which reflects a slightly different reading of the same letters. In each case the nations are taunted: whatever they attempt will end in their ruin.

decisions.choice: be shattered: commands that announce what will surely happen
decisions.reason: The commands mock the nations: arm yourselves if you will, the result will be your defeat. The repeated "be shattered" makes the outcome certain. The prophet now addresses the nations, answering the threat of verses 7-8 with the hope of the name Immanuel (verse 10).

decisions.choice: arm for war (Balanced); get ready for battle (Readable)
decisions.reason: To gird oneself is to fasten on belt and weapons for battle. Literal keeps "gird yourselves".

source.text: עֻ֥צוּ עֵצָ֖ה וְתֻפָ֑ר דַּבְּר֤וּ דָבָר֙ וְלֹ֣א יָק֔וּם כִּ֥י עִמָּ֖נוּ אֵֽל׃ס

records.literal_gloss: Plan a plan, and it will be frustrated; speak a word, and not it will stand, for with us God.

en.L: Plan a plan, and it will be frustrated; \q speak a word, and it will not stand; for with us [is] God.
en.B: Draw up your plans; they will be undone. \q Give the order; it will not stand. For God is with us.
en.R: Make your plans, but they will fail. \q Give your orders, but they will never happen. For God is with us!

es.L: {{plural_you:Tracen|Trazad}} un plan, y será frustrado; \q {{plural_you:digan|decid}} una palabra, y no se mantendrá; porque con nosotros [está] Dios.
es.B: {{plural_you:Hagan sus planes|Haced vuestros planes}}; serán deshechos. \q {{plural_you:Den|Dad}} la orden; no se cumplirá. Porque Dios está con nosotros.
es.R: {{plural_you:Hagan sus planes|Haced vuestros planes}}, pero fracasarán. \q {{plural_you:Den sus órdenes|Dad vuestras órdenes}}, pero nunca se cumplirán. ¡Porque Dios está con nosotros!

sw.L: Fanyeni shauri, nalo litabatilika; \q semeni neno, nalo halitasimama; kwa maana Mungu [yuko] pamoja nasi.
sw.B: Pangeni mipango yenu; itavunjwa. \q Toeni amri; haitasimama. Kwa maana Mungu yuko pamoja nasi.
sw.R: Fanyeni mipango yenu, lakini itashindwa. \q Toeni amri zenu, lakini hazitatimia kamwe. Kwa maana Mungu yuko pamoja nasi!

decisions.choice: God is with us: the words of the name Immanuel
decisions.reason: The last words of the verse are the two words that make the name Immanuel (7:14; verse 8). What was a name becomes a confession of faith: the nations' plans fail because God is with his people.

decisions.choice: speak a word: issue a decree, give an order
decisions.reason: "Word" here is a decision announced by a ruler. Like the plans, it will not "stand", that is, it will not come about (compare 7:7, "it will not stand").

decisions.choice: Dios está con nosotros
decisions.reason: The closing words are the two words of the name Immanuel; every level says "Dios está con nosotros", the meaning given for Emanuel in 7:14 R and Matthew 1:23, so the echo can be heard.

decisions.choice: "Mungu [yuko] pamoja nasi"
decisions.reason: The same words as Readable's meaning of the name Imanueli at 7:14, so the reader hears the name (m1).

en.L: For thus {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to me with strength of the hand, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} warned me against walking in the way of this people, saying,
en.B: For this is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to me while {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} hand held me hard, warning me not to follow the way of this people:
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} took firm hold of me and spoke to me. He warned me not to live the way these people live. He said,

es.B: Porque esto es lo que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} me dijo mientras {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} mano me sujetaba con fuerza, advirtiéndome que no siguiera el camino de este pueblo:
es.R: {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} me tomó con fuerza y me habló. Me advirtió que no viviera como vive esta gente. Me dijo:

sw.B: Kwa maana haya ndiyo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} aliyoniambia mkono {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} ulipokuwa umenishika kwa nguvu, akinionya nisifuate njia ya watu hawa:
sw.R: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alinishika kwa nguvu na kusema nami. Alinionya nisiishi kama watu hawa wanavyoishi. Alisema,

decisions.choice: the strength of the hand: the LORD's hand gripping the prophet
decisions.reason: The "hand" of the LORD on a prophet means his power taking hold of him to give a message (Ezekiel 3:14; 2 Kings 3:15). Here it stresses how forcefully the warning came.

decisions.choice: he warned me: the received Hebrew text, "instructed, admonished me"
alternatives: he turned me away from walking
decisions.reason: The Hebrew reads "he instructed" or "warned me" not to walk in the people's way. The Great Isaiah Scroll (1QIsa-a) has a form of the verb "turn aside": "he turned me aside from walking". The sense is close either way.

decisions.choice: took firm hold of me and spoke to me
decisions.reason: Readable breaks the verse into short sentences and states the idiom of the hand plainly.

source.text: לֹא־תֹאמְר֣וּן קֶ֔שֶׁר לְכֹ֧ל אֲשֶׁר־יֹאמַ֛ר הָעָ֥ם הַזֶּ֖ה קָ֑שֶׁר וְאֶת־מוֹרָא֥וֹ לֹֽא־תִֽירְא֖וּ וְלֹ֥א תַעֲרִֽיצוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: Not you must say conspiracy to all that says the people the this conspiracy; and its fear not you must fear and not you must dread.

en.L: "You must not call conspiracy all that this people calls conspiracy, \q and its fear you must not fear, and you must not dread [it].
en.B: "Do not call something a plot just because this people calls it a plot. \q What frightens them must not frighten you; do not tremble at it.
en.R: "Do not think there is a plot just because these people say there is. \q Do not be afraid of the things they fear. Do not be terrified.

es.L: «No {{plural_you:llamen|llaméis}} conspiración a todo lo que este pueblo llama conspiración, \q y no {{plural_you:teman|temáis}} lo que él teme, ni {{plural_you:tengan|tengáis}} pavor.
es.B: «No {{plural_you:llamen|llaméis}} conspiración a algo solo porque este pueblo lo llama conspiración. \q Lo que a ellos los asusta no {{plural_you:debe asustarlos a ustedes|debe asustaros a vosotros}}; no {{plural_you:tiemblen|tembléis}} por ello.
es.R: «No {{plural_you:piensen|penséis}} que hay una conspiración solo porque esta gente dice que la hay. \q No {{plural_you:tengan|tengáis}} miedo de lo que ellos temen. No {{plural_you:se aterroricen|os aterroricéis}}.

sw.L: "Msiite njama yote ambayo watu hawa wanaiita njama, \q wala msiogope hofu yao, wala msitishike.
sw.B: "Msiite jambo njama kwa sababu tu watu hawa wanaliita njama. \q Kinachowaogopesha wao kisiwaogopeshe ninyi; msikitetemekee.
sw.R: "Msidhani kwamba kuna njama kwa sababu tu watu hawa wanasema kwamba ipo. \q Msiogope mambo wanayoyaogopa. Msiwe na hofu.

decisions.choice: conspiracy: a plot or treacherous alliance
decisions.reason: The word means a conspiracy or a binding together against someone. The people may have seen plots everywhere: the alliance of Aram and Israel against Judah (7:2, 5-6), or rumors of treason at home. The prophet and those with him are not to be ruled by the panic of the crowd.

decisions.choice: you: plural, the prophet and those who listen to him
decisions.reason: The commands are plural; they are addressed to Isaiah together with the disciples of verse 16. First Peter 3:14-15 echoes verses 12-13: do not fear what they fear, but set apart the Lord as holy.

source.text: אֶת־יְהוָ֥ה צְבָא֖וֹת אֹת֣וֹ תַקְדִּ֑ישׁוּ וְה֥וּא מוֹרַאֲכֶ֖ם וְה֥וּא מַֽעֲרִֽצְכֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: Yahweh of hosts, him you will regard as holy, and he [will be] your fear, and he [will be] your dread.

en.L: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} of hosts, {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} you shall regard as holy, \q and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} [shall be] your fear, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} [shall be] your dread.
en.B: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies is the one you must treat as holy. \q Let {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} be the one you fear, let {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} be the one who makes you tremble.
en.R: Instead, treat {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies as holy. \q He is the one you should fear and stand in awe of.

es.L: {{divine_name:Al SEÑOR|A Yahvé}} de los ejércitos, a {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} {{plural_you:tendrán|tendréis}} por santo, \q y {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} [será] {{plural_you:su temor|vuestro temor}}, y {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} [será] {{plural_you:su pavor|vuestro pavor}}.
es.B: {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} de los Ejércitos es a quien {{plural_you:deben|debéis}} tratar como santo. \q Que {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} sea a quien {{plural_you:teman|temáis}}, que {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} sea quien {{plural_you:los haga|os haga}} temblar.
es.R: Más bien, {{plural_you:traten|tratad}} {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}} de los Ejércitos como santo. \q Él es a quien {{plural_you:deben|debéis}} temer y reverenciar.

sw.L: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} wa majeshi, {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} ndiye mtakayemtakasa, \q na {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} [atakuwa] hofu yenu, na {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} [atakuwa] kitisho chenu.
sw.B: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} wa majeshi ndiye mnayepaswa kumheshimu kuwa mtakatifu. \q Yeye awe ndiye mnayemwogopa, {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} awe ndiye anayewatetemesha.
sw.R: Badala yake, mheshimuni {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} wa majeshi kuwa mtakatifu. \q Yeye ndiye mnayepaswa kumwogopa na kumcha.

decisions.choice: regard as holy: treat as set apart, honor as the Holy One
decisions.reason: To regard the LORD as holy is to give him the honor and trust due to the Holy One (6:3), instead of fearing human threats. The same root gives "sanctuary" in verse 14.

decisions.choice: your fear ... your dread: the right object of fear
decisions.reason: The words "fear" and "dread" repeat verse 12. The fear the people feel toward enemies belongs to the LORD alone; whoever fears him need fear nothing else.

decisions.choice: Instead
decisions.reason: Readable marks the contrast with verse 12, which the Hebrew makes by putting the LORD first in the sentence.

source.text: וְהָיָ֖ה לְמִקְדָּ֑שׁ וּלְאֶ֣בֶן נֶ֠גֶף וּלְצ֨וּר מִכְשׁ֜וֹל לִשְׁנֵ֨י בָתֵּ֤י יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ לְפַ֣ח וּלְמוֹקֵ֔שׁ לְיוֹשֵׁ֖ב יְרוּשָׁלִָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And he will become a sanctuary, and a stone of striking and a rock of stumbling for the two houses of Israel, a trap and a snare for [the] inhabitant of Jerusalem.

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will become a sanctuary, \q and a stone of striking and a rock of stumbling for the two houses of Israel, a trap and a snare for the inhabitants of Jerusalem.
en.B: He will be a holy place of refuge, \q but also a stone that people strike against and a rock they trip over, for both houses of Israel; a trap and a snare for those who live in Jerusalem.
en.R: He will be a safe and holy place. \q But for both kingdoms of Israel {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will also be like a stone that people trip on, a rock that makes them fall. For the people of Jerusalem {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will be like a trap or a net that catches them.

es.L: Y {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} será santuario, \q y piedra de tropiezo y roca de caída para las dos casas de Israel, trampa y lazo para los habitantes de Jerusalén.
es.B: Él será un lugar santo de refugio, \q pero también una piedra contra la que la gente tropieza y una roca con la que cae, para las dos casas de Israel; una trampa y un lazo para los que viven en Jerusalén.
es.R: Él será un lugar seguro y santo. \q Pero para los dos reinos de Israel {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} será también como una piedra en la que la gente tropieza, una roca que la hace caer. Para la gente de Jerusalén {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} será como una trampa o una red que la atrapa.

sw.L: Naye atakuwa patakatifu, \q na jiwe la kugonga na mwamba wa kujikwaa kwa nyumba zote mbili za Israeli, mtego na tanzi kwa wakaaji wa Yerusalemu.
sw.B: Atakuwa mahali patakatifu pa kukimbilia, \q lakini pia jiwe ambalo watu hujigonga juu yake na mwamba wanaojikwaa juu yake, kwa nyumba zote mbili za Israeli; mtego na tanzi kwa wakaaji wa Yerusalemu.
sw.R: Atakuwa mahali salama na patakatifu. \q Lakini kwa falme zote mbili za Israeli atakuwa pia kama jiwe ambalo watu hujikwaa juu yake, mwamba unaowaangusha. Kwa watu wa Yerusalemu atakuwa kama mtego au wavu unaowanasa.

decisions.choice: sanctuary: a holy place, a place of refuge
alternatives: snare (a proposed change to the text)
decisions.reason: The word means a holy place, from the root of "regard as holy" (verse 13). For those who fear him, the LORD himself is a place of safety (compare Ezekiel 11:16). The Septuagint reads the verse differently, "you will not meet him as a stone of stumbling". Some have suggested a different word, "snare", but the received text has "sanctuary".

decisions.choice: a stone of striking and a rock of stumbling: quoted in the New Testament of Christ
decisions.reason: The same LORD who is a refuge to some is a stone others trip over. Paul joins this verse to 28:16 in Romans 9:33, and Peter quotes it in 1 Peter 2:8, both applying it to Jesus, whom many stumbled over.

decisions.choice: the two houses of Israel: the northern kingdom of Israel and the southern kingdom of Judah
decisions.reason: Both kingdoms descended from Jacob, called Israel; at this time they were enemies (7:1).

decisions.choice: both kingdoms of Israel
decisions.reason: Readable says "kingdoms" for "houses", which here means the two royal states. It also puts the pictures as comparisons ("like a stone").

decisions.choice: "jiwe la kugonga na mwamba wa kujikwaa"
alternatives: "jiwe la kujikwaa na mwamba wa kuangusha"
decisions.reason: The words are close to those Romans 9:33 and 1 Peter 2:8 use when they quote this verse (m2), so the reader can see the quotation.

records.literal_gloss: And will stumble over them many, and they will fall and be broken, and be ensnared and be captured.

en.L: And many will stumble over them, \q and they will fall and be broken, and they will be snared and be captured."
en.B: Many will stumble on them and fall; \q they will be broken, caught in the snare, and carried off."
en.R: Many people will trip over it and fall. \q They will be hurt badly. They will be caught and taken away."

es.L: Y muchos tropezarán en ellos, \q y caerán y serán quebrantados, y serán enlazados y apresados».
es.B: Muchos tropezarán con ellos y caerán; \q serán quebrantados, atrapados en el lazo y llevados cautivos».
es.R: Mucha gente tropezará con ella y caerá. \q Quedarán muy lastimados. Serán atrapados y llevados prisioneros».

sw.L: Na wengi watajikwaa juu yake, \q nao wataanguka na kuvunjika, nao watanaswa na kukamatwa."
sw.B: Wengi watajikwaa juu yake na kuanguka; \q watavunjika, watanaswa mtegoni na kuchukuliwa."
sw.R: Watu wengi watajikwaa juu yake na kuanguka. \q Wataumia vibaya. Watanaswa na kuchukuliwa mateka."

decisions.choice: over them: over the stone and the rock, or among them
decisions.reason: "Them" most likely points back to the stone and rock, trap and snare of verse 14. It could also mean "many among them" will stumble.

decisions.choice: be captured: be taken, like an animal in a trap or a captive in war
decisions.reason: The five verbs follow the pictures of verse 14: stumble and fall on the stone, be broken, be caught in the snare, be taken.

source.text: צ֖וֹר תְּעוּדָ֑ה חֲת֥וֹם תּוֹרָ֖ה בְּלִמֻּדָֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: Bind up [the] testimony; seal [the] instruction among my disciples.

en.L: Bind up [the] testimony; \q seal [the] instruction among my disciples.
en.B: Wrap up the testimony, \q and put a seal on the instruction among my disciples.
en.R: Tie up the message that God has given, \q and seal up the teaching. Keep it safe among my followers.

es.L: Ata el testimonio; \q sella la instrucción entre mis discípulos.
es.B: Envuelve el testimonio \q y pon un sello a la instrucción entre mis discípulos.
es.R: Ata el mensaje que Dios ha dado \q y sella la enseñanza. Guárdala bien entre mis seguidores.

sw.L: Funga ushuhuda; \q tia muhuri mafundisho kati ya wanafunzi wangu.
sw.B: Ukunje ushuhuda, \q na uyatie muhuri mafundisho kati ya wanafunzi wangu.
sw.R: Funga ujumbe ambao Mungu ametoa, \q na uyatie muhuri mafundisho. Yahifadhi salama kati ya wafuasi wangu.

decisions.choice: bind up ... seal: to close and secure a written document
decisions.reason: A scroll was tied and sealed so that it could not be changed and would serve later as proof (Jeremiah 32:10-14). The prophet's message is kept until events show it to be true (compare 30:8).

decisions.choice: my disciples: the prophet's followers, or those taught by the LORD
decisions.reason: The speaker is not named. It may be Isaiah, speaking of the circle who accepted his message, or the LORD, speaking of those he has taught (54:13). The disciples are the faithful few, set apart from "this people" (verses 11-12).

decisions.choice: testimony and instruction: the prophet's message as a witness and a teaching
decisions.reason: "Testimony" is the message confirmed before witnesses (verse 2); "instruction" is the LORD's teaching given through the prophet. The two words return in verse 20.

decisions.choice: the message that God has given; Keep it safe
decisions.reason: Readable explains "testimony" and spells out the purpose of the sealing.

decisions.choice: "mafundisho" for *torah* in 8:16 and 8:20
decisions.reason: The prophet's sealed message is teaching (m3), as at 1:10 and 2:3, so every level says "mafundisho".

source.text: וְחִכִּ֨יתִי֙ לַיהוָ֔ה הַמַּסְתִּ֥יר פָּנָ֖יו מִבֵּ֣ית יַעֲקֹ֑ב וְקִוֵּ֖יתִֽי־לֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: And I will wait for Yahweh, who is hiding his face from the house of Jacob, and I will wait eagerly for him.

en.L: And I will wait for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, who hides {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} face from the house of Jacob, \q and I will hope for {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.B: I will wait on {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} while {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} keeps {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} face hidden from the house of Jacob; \q I will look to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} in hope.
en.R: I will wait for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} to act, even though {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has turned away from the people of Israel. \q I will keep trusting in {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

es.L: Y esperaré {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}}, que esconde {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} rostro de la casa de Jacob, \q y en {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} esperaré.
es.B: Esperaré {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}} mientras {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} mantiene {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} rostro escondido de la casa de Jacob; \q pondré en {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} mi esperanza.
es.R: Esperaré a que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} actúe, aunque {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} se ha apartado del pueblo de Israel. \q Seguiré confiando en {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}.

sw.L: Nami nitamngoja {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, anayeuficha uso {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} mbali na nyumba ya Yakobo, \q nami nitamtumaini.
sw.B: Nitamngoja {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} ingawa anauficha uso {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} mbali na nyumba ya Yakobo; \q nitamtazamia kwa tumaini.
sw.R: Nitamngoja {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} atende, ingawa amewapa kisogo watu wa Israeli. \q Nitaendelea kumtumaini.

decisions.choice: hiding his face: withdrawing favor and help
decisions.reason: When the LORD hides his face, he holds back his blessing and lets his people bear the results of their sin (Deuteronomy 31:17-18; Psalm 30:8). The prophet waits for the day he will show his face again.

decisions.choice: I will hope for him: words used in Hebrews 2:13
decisions.reason: The Septuagint form of this line, "I will trust in him", is quoted in Hebrews 2:13, together with verse 18, as words of Christ.

decisions.choice: the people of Israel
decisions.reason: "The house of Jacob" means the people descended from Jacob, who was also called Israel. Readable also explains the idiom of the hidden face.

source.text: הִנֵּ֣ה אָנֹכִ֗י וְהַיְלָדִים֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר נָֽתַן־לִ֣י יְהוָ֔ה לְאֹת֥וֹת וּלְמוֹפְתִ֖ים בְּיִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל מֵעִם֙ יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֔וֹת הַשֹּׁכֵ֖ן בְּהַ֥ר צִיּֽוֹן׃ס

records.literal_gloss: Look, I and the children whom has given to me Yahweh [are] for signs and for portents in Israel from with Yahweh of hosts who dwells on the mountain of Zion.

en.L: Look, I and the children whom {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has given to me [are] for signs and for portents in Israel \q from {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of hosts, who dwells on Mount Zion.
en.B: Here I am with the children {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has given me. We are signs and omens in Israel \q from {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies, who makes {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} home on Mount Zion.
en.R: I and the children {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has given me are signs to warn Israel. \q They come from {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies, who lives on Mount Zion.

es.L: He aquí, yo y los hijos que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} me ha dado [somos] señales y prodigios en Israel \q de parte {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} de los ejércitos, que habita en el monte Sion.
es.B: Aquí estoy yo con los hijos que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} me ha dado. Somos señales y presagios en Israel \q de parte {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} de los Ejércitos, que tiene {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} morada en el monte Sion.
es.R: Yo y los hijos que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} me ha dado somos señales para advertir a Israel. \q Vienen {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} de los Ejércitos, que vive en el monte Sion.

sw.L: Tazama, mimi na watoto ambao {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} amenipa [tu] ishara na ajabu katika Israeli \q kutoka kwa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} wa majeshi, akaaye katika mlima Sayuni.
sw.B: Niko hapa pamoja na watoto ambao {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} amenipa. Sisi ni ishara na maonyo katika Israeli \q kutoka kwa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} wa majeshi, anayeishi katika mlima Sayuni.
sw.R: Mimi na watoto ambao {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} amenipa ni ishara za kuwaonya Israeli. \q Ishara hizo zinatoka kwa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} wa majeshi, anayeishi katika mlima Sayuni.

decisions.choice: the children ... signs and portents: Isaiah's sons and their names
decisions.reason: Isaiah's sons carry messages in their names: Shear-jashub, "a remnant will return" (7:3), and Maher-shalal-hash-baz, "spoil hurries" (verse 3). Isaiah's own name means "the LORD saves". The family itself is a message to Israel.

decisions.choice: I and the children: quoted in Hebrews 2:13
decisions.reason: Hebrews 2:13 quotes these words, with verse 17, as spoken by Christ about those God has given him.

decisions.choice: who dwells on Mount Zion: the LORD present among his people
decisions.reason: Though he hides his face (verse 17), the LORD still dwells in Zion, at the temple in Jerusalem. That is the ground of the prophet's hope.

decisions.choice: "Tazama, mimi na watoto ambao BWANA amenipa"
decisions.reason: Kept close to the Swahili of Hebrews 2:13, which quotes these words (m2); the prophet is speaking, so there is no deity span on "mimi" here.

source.text: וְכִֽי־יֹאמְר֣וּ אֲלֵיכֶ֗ם דִּרְשׁ֤וּ אֶל־הָאֹבוֹת֙ וְאֶל־הַיִּדְּעֹנִ֔ים הַֽמְצַפְצְפִ֖ים וְהַמַּהְגִּ֑ים הֲלוֹא־עַם֙ אֶל־אֱלֹהָ֣יו יִדְרֹ֔שׁ בְּעַ֥ד הַחַיִּ֖ים אֶל־הַמֵּתִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: And when they say to you, consult the necromancers and the soothsayers who whisper and who mutter, not a people to its God will it consult? For the living, to the dead?

en.L: And when they say to you, "Consult the spirits of the dead and the spiritists who chirp and who mutter," \q should not a people consult its God? \q On behalf of the living, [consult] the dead?
en.B: When they tell you, "Seek out the ghosts and the familiar spirits that chirp and moan," \q should a people not seek its own God? \q Should they go to the dead on behalf of the living?
en.R: People will tell you, "Ask the spirits of the dead for advice. Go to those who whisper and mumble." \q But should people not ask their own God for help? \q Why ask the dead to help the living?

es.L: Y cuando {{plural_you:les|os}} digan: «{{plural_you:Consulten|Consultad}} a los espíritus de los muertos y a los adivinos que susurran y murmuran», \q ¿no consultará un pueblo a su Dios? \q ¿Por los vivos [consultará] a los muertos?
es.B: Cuando {{plural_you:les|os}} digan: «{{plural_you:Busquen|Buscad}} a los fantasmas y a los espíritus que pían y gimen», \q ¿no debe un pueblo buscar a su propio Dios? \q ¿Acudirán a los muertos en favor de los vivos?
es.R: La gente {{plural_you:les|os}} dirá: «{{plural_you:Pidan|Pedid}} consejo a los espíritus de los muertos. {{plural_you:Vayan|Id}} a los que susurran y murmuran». \q Pero ¿no debe la gente pedir ayuda a su propio Dios? \q ¿Por qué pedir a los muertos que ayuden a los vivos?

sw.L: Na watakapowaambia, "Waulizeni wapunga pepo na wachawi wanaolialia na kunong'ona," \q je, watu hawapaswi kumwuliza Mungu wao? \q Kwa ajili ya walio hai, [wawaulize] wafu?
sw.B: Watakapowaambia, "Watafuteni mizimu na pepo wanaolia kama ndege na kuguna," \q je, watu hawapaswi kumtafuta Mungu wao wenyewe? \q Je, waende kwa wafu kwa ajili ya walio hai?
sw.R: Watu watawaambia, "Ulizeni roho za wafu ushauri. Nendeni kwa wale wanaonong'ona na kunung'unika." \q Lakini je, watu hawapaswi kumwomba Mungu wao msaada? \q Kwa nini waulize wafu wawasaidie walio hai?

decisions.choice: spirits of the dead and spiritists: ways of seeking messages from the dead
decisions.reason: The first word means the ghost of a dead person or the one who calls it up (1 Samuel 28:7-8); the second means one who "knows", a familiar spirit or a medium. The Law of Moses forbids both (Leviticus 19:31; Deuteronomy 18:10-12).

decisions.choice: chirp and mutter: the faint sounds thought to come from the dead
decisions.reason: The words describe bird-like chirping and low muttering, the voices heard in the practice of calling up the dead (compare 29:4).

decisions.choice: should not a people consult its God: the prophet's answer
alternatives: should not a people consult its gods (still the people speaking)
decisions.reason: Read this way, the question answers the people's advice: Israel should seek the living God, not the dead. The word for God can also mean "gods" or spirits (1 Samuel 28:13), and some read the question as part of what the people say: "Should not a people consult its gods, the dead on behalf of the living?"

source.text: לְתוֹרָ֖ה וְלִתְעוּדָ֑ה אִם־לֹ֤א יֹֽאמְרוּ֙ כַּדָּבָ֣ר הַזֶּ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר אֵֽין־ל֖וֹ שָֽׁחַר׃

records.literal_gloss: To [the] instruction and to [the] testimony! If not they will speak according to the word the this, that there is not for it dawn.

en.L: To [the] instruction and to [the] testimony! \q If they do not speak according to this word, [it is one] for which there is no dawn.
en.B: To the instruction and the testimony! \q Those who do not speak in keeping with this word have no dawn before them.
en.R: Turn to the teaching and the message God has given! \q People who do not speak by this message will never see the light of morning.

es.L: ¡A la instrucción y al testimonio! \q Si no hablan conforme a esta palabra, [es algo] para lo cual no hay aurora.
es.B: ¡A la instrucción y al testimonio! \q Los que no hablen de acuerdo con esta palabra no tienen aurora delante de ellos.
es.R: ¡{{plural_you:Vuélvanse|Volveos}} a la enseñanza y al mensaje que Dios ha dado! \q Los que no hablen según este mensaje nunca verán la luz de la mañana.

sw.L: Kwa mafundisho na kwa ushuhuda! \q Kama hawatasema sawasawa na neno hili, [ni wale] wasio na mapambazuko.
sw.B: Rudini kwa mafundisho na ushuhuda! \q Wale wasiosema sawasawa na neno hili hawana mapambazuko mbele yao.
sw.R: Rudini kwa mafundisho na ujumbe ambao Mungu ametoa! \q Watu wasiosema kufuatana na ujumbe huu hawataiona kamwe nuru ya asubuhi.

decisions.choice: to the instruction and to the testimony: back to the sealed message of verse 16
decisions.reason: The cry calls the people to the LORD's word given through the prophet, instead of the voices of the dead (verse 19).

decisions.choice: no dawn: no light, no hope of a new day
alternatives: no power to charm (from a similar word)
decisions.reason: "Dawn" is the morning that ends the night. Those who reject the LORD's word are left in darkness with no morning ahead, the darkness described in verses 21-22. Some take the clause as "surely they will speak this way, which has no dawn in it".

decisions.choice: Turn to; the message God has given
decisions.reason: Readable supplies the verb and explains "testimony" as in verse 16.

source.text: וְעָ֥בַר בָּ֖הּ נִקְשֶׁ֣ה וְרָעֵ֑ב וְהָיָ֨ה כִֽי־יִרְעַ֜ב וְהִתְקַצַּ֗ף וְקִלֵּ֧ל בְּמַלְכּ֛וֹ וּבֵאלֹהָ֖יו וּפָנָ֥ה לְמָֽעְלָה׃

records.literal_gloss: And he will pass through it hard-pressed and hungry, and it will be when he is hungry, and he will be enraged and he will curse by his king and by his God, and he will turn upwards.

en.L: And [he] will pass through it, hard-pressed and hungry; \q and when he is hungry, he will be enraged and curse by his king and by his God, and he will turn [his face] upward.
en.B: They will roam through the land, worn down and hungry. \q When hunger gnaws at them, they will rage and curse their king and their God, and turn their faces upward.
en.R: The people will wander through the land, troubled and hungry. \q Their hunger will make them angry. They will curse their king and their God, and they will look up to the sky.

es.L: Y pasará por ella, angustiado y hambriento; \q y cuando tenga hambre, se enfurecerá y maldecirá por su rey y por su Dios, y volverá [el rostro] hacia arriba.
es.B: Andarán errantes por la tierra, agotados y hambrientos. \q Cuando el hambre los atormente, se enfurecerán y maldecirán a su rey y a su Dios, y alzarán el rostro hacia arriba.
es.R: La gente andará errante por el país, angustiada y con hambre. \q El hambre los pondrá furiosos. Maldecirán a su rey y a su Dios, y mirarán hacia el cielo.

sw.L: Naye atapita ndani yake, akiwa amesongwa na mwenye njaa; \q na itakuwa atakapoona njaa, atakasirika na kumlaani mfalme wake na Mungu wake, naye atageuza [uso wake] juu.
sw.B: Watatangatanga katika nchi, wakiwa wamechoka na wenye njaa. \q Njaa itakapowauma, watakasirika na kumlaani mfalme wao na Mungu wao, na kuinua nyuso zao juu.
sw.R: Watu watatangatanga katika nchi, wakiwa na taabu na njaa. \q Njaa yao itawakasirisha. Watamlaani mfalme wao na Mungu wao, nao watatazama juu angani.

decisions.choice: he will pass through it: the people, spoken of as one person, wandering through the land
decisions.reason: The subject is not named. It is most likely the people who rejected the LORD's word (verses 19-20), spoken of as one; "it" is the land.

decisions.choice: curse by his king and by his God: curse king and God, or swear by them
alternatives: curse by his king and his gods
decisions.reason: The verb with this preposition may mean to curse the king and God in bitterness, or to utter curses in their name. "His God" may also be "his gods". Either way the starving people turn against the very ones they should look to.

decisions.choice: they; the people
decisions.reason: The Hebrew speaks of the people as "he". Balanced and Readable use "they" and Readable names the people.

source.text: וְאֶל־אֶ֖רֶץ יַבִּ֑יט וְהִנֵּ֨ה צָרָ֤ה וַחֲשֵׁכָה֙ מְע֣וּף צוּקָ֔ה וַאֲפֵלָ֖ה מְנֻדָּֽח׃

records.literal_gloss: And to [the] earth he will look, and look, distress and darkness, gloom of anguish; and [into] thick darkness [he is] thrust.

en.L: And to [the] earth he will look, \q and look, distress and darkness, [the] gloom of anguish; and [into] thick darkness [he will be] driven.
en.B: They will stare at the ground, \q and there will be trouble and darkness, the dimness of anguish; into thick darkness they are driven.
en.R: Then they will look down at the earth. \q But they will see only trouble and darkness and terrible gloom. They will be pushed into deep darkness.

es.L: Y a la tierra mirará, \q y he aquí angustia y tinieblas, la oscuridad de la aflicción; y [a las] densas tinieblas [será] empujado.
es.B: Fijarán la mirada en el suelo, \q y habrá angustia y tinieblas, la penumbra de la aflicción; a la oscuridad profunda serán arrojados.
es.R: Luego mirarán hacia la tierra. \q Pero solo verán angustia, tinieblas y una oscuridad terrible. Serán empujados a una oscuridad profunda.

sw.L: Naye ataitazama nchi, \q na tazama, dhiki na giza, utusitusi wa uchungu; naye [atasukumwa katika] giza nene.
sw.B: Watakodolea macho ardhi, \q na kutakuwa na taabu na giza, kiza cha uchungu; nao wanasukumwa katika giza nene.
sw.R: Kisha watatazama chini ardhini. \q Lakini wataona taabu tu na giza na huzuni kuu. Watasukumwa katika giza nene.

decisions.choice: to the earth ... darkness: no help above or below
decisions.reason: Looking up (verse 21) and looking down both find nothing but darkness. The scene recalls the darkness sent on Egypt (Exodus 10:22) and the warning of Deuteronomy 28:29.

decisions.choice: thrust: driven into darkness
decisions.reason: The last word means "driven" or "banished". It most likely means the people are driven into the darkness; it could also describe the darkness itself as spreading.

source.text: כִּ֣י לֹ֣א מוּעָף֮ לַאֲשֶׁ֣ר מוּצָ֣ק לָהּ֒ כָּעֵ֣ת הָרִאשׁ֗וֹן הֵקַ֞ל אַ֤רְצָה זְבֻלוּן֙ וְאַ֣רְצָה נַפְתָּלִ֔י וְהָאַחֲר֖וֹן הִכְבִּ֑יד דֶּ֤רֶךְ הַיָּם֙ עֵ֣בֶר הַיַּרְדֵּ֔ן גְּלִ֖יל הַגּוֹיִֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: For not gloom to [that] which distress [belonged] to it. As the time the former he treated with contempt [the] land of Zebulun and [the] land of Naphtali, and the latter he will honor the way of the sea, [the] other side of the Jordan, Galilee of the nations.

en.L: But [there will be] no gloom for her who [was] in distress. As [in] the former time {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} treated with contempt the land of Zebulun and the land of Naphtali, [so] the latter [time] {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will make glorious the way of the sea, beyond the Jordan, Galilee of the nations.
en.B: Yet the land in anguish will not be left in gloom. At first {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} brought low the land of Zebulun and the land of Naphtali, but afterward {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will bring honor to the way of the sea, the land beyond the Jordan, Galilee of the nations.
en.R: But the darkness will not last for the land that suffered. In the past God let the lands of Zebulun and Naphtali be put to shame. But later {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will bring honor to the land along the road to the sea, the land on the other side of the Jordan River, and Galilee, where many foreign people live.

es.L: Pero no [habrá] oscuridad para la que [estaba] en angustia. Como en el tiempo primero {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} trató con desprecio la tierra de Zabulón y la tierra de Neftalí, [así] en el postrero hará glorioso el camino del mar, al otro lado del Jordán, Galilea de las naciones.
es.B: Pero la tierra angustiada no quedará en tinieblas. Al principio {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} humilló la tierra de Zabulón y la tierra de Neftalí, pero después honrará el camino del mar, la tierra al otro lado del Jordán, Galilea de las naciones.
es.R: Pero la oscuridad no durará para la tierra que sufrió. En el pasado Dios dejó que las tierras de Zabulón y Neftalí fueran humilladas. Pero más tarde {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} honrará la tierra junto al camino del mar, la tierra al otro lado del río Jordán y Galilea, donde vive mucha gente extranjera.

sw.L: Lakini hakutakuwa na utusitusi kwake yeye aliyekuwa katika dhiki. Kama wakati wa kwanza alivyoidharau nchi ya Zabuloni na nchi ya Naftali, [hivyo] wakati wa mwisho ataitukuza njia ya bahari, ng'ambo ya Yordani, Galilaya ya mataifa.
sw.B: Lakini nchi iliyokuwa katika uchungu haitaachwa gizani. Mwanzoni aliishusha nchi ya Zabuloni na nchi ya Naftali, lakini baadaye ataiheshimu njia ya bahari, nchi iliyo ng'ambo ya Yordani, Galilaya ya mataifa.
sw.R: Lakini giza halitadumu kwa nchi iliyoteseka. Zamani Mungu aliziacha nchi za Zabuloni na Naftali ziaibishwe. Lakini baadaye ataiheshimu nchi iliyo kando ya njia iendayo baharini, nchi iliyo ng'ambo ya mto Yordani, na Galilaya, wanakoishi watu wengi wa mataifa mengine.

decisions.choice: This verse is 8:23 in the Hebrew text, 9:1 in Bibles that follow the Latin and later numbering
decisions.reason: The Hebrew text ends chapter 8 with this verse and begins chapter 9 with "The people who walked in darkness". Many Bibles number this verse 9:1, so their 9:1-21 is 8:23 and 9:1-20 here. Open Word Bible follows the numbering of the Hebrew text it translates. The verse belongs with 9:1: it turns the darkness of 8:22 into the promise of light.

decisions.choice: treated with contempt ... will make glorious: humbling then honor
alternatives: the latter one made it heavy (oppressed it)
decisions.reason: The first verb means to make light of, the second to make heavy or glorious; they are opposites. The northern lands were the first to be stripped by Assyria in 732 BC (2 Kings 15:29), but the latter time will bring them honor. The second verb could also mean "made heavy", that is, oppressed further, but the contrast and the light of 9:1 point to honor.

decisions.choice: the way of the sea, beyond the Jordan, Galilee of the nations: the far north, quoted in Matthew
decisions.reason: "The way of the sea" is the road through Galilee toward the Mediterranean; "Galilee of the nations" is the northern region with many non-Israelite people. Matthew 4:15-16 quotes this verse with 9:1 as fulfilled when Jesus began to preach in Galilee, in Capernaum by the lake, in the land of Zebulun and Naphtali.

decisions.choice: God; where many foreign people live
decisions.reason: The Hebrew does not name the one who acts; the context shows it is the LORD. Readable names God and explains "Galilee of the nations".

decisions.choice: Zabulón ... Neftalí ... el camino del mar ... al otro lado del Jordán ... Galilea de las naciones
decisions.reason: Matthew 4:15 quotes this verse; its key terms are kept (Zabulón, Neftalí, camino del mar, al otro lado del Jordán), but the Hebrew goyim is "las naciones" as everywhere in Isaiah, where Matthew has "los gentiles". This is Hebrew 8:23, 9:1 in many Bibles.

decisions.choice: "Zabuloni", "Naftali", "ng'ambo ya Yordani", "Galilaya ya mataifa"
decisions.reason: The names and phrases follow the Swahili of Matthew 4:15, which quotes this verse (m3).
